ops.title: VM panic-mitigation validation runs should use a 10-minute window, not long soaks — the failure mode is near-instant so 10 min is a decisive pass.
ops.body:
For fusekit's tart VM mitigation validation (`scripts/vm/vmctl run scenarios/validate-mitigation.sh`), a **10-minute** clean window is a decisive pass — do not run 120-minute (or longer) soaks.

**Why:** the unmitigated holder kernel-panics the guest in ~2 seconds, 28/28 deterministically. A clean 10-minute run is hundreds of times the failure latency, so it fully validates the mitigation. Long soaks add wall-clock cost without adding confidence. The user called an in-progress 72-minute run a pass and set 10 min as the standing bar.

**How to apply:** the harness default `VMCTL_RUN_TIMEOUT_MIN` is now `10` (fusekit `scripts/vm/lib.sh`); leave it. Only raise it per-invocation for a deliberate extended soak. Relates to the [[macos-nfs-vinvalbuf2-panic]] mitigation work and the reusable VM framework in [[fusekit-content-over-rpc]].
